description: Sabotages for win-authorization-sys's allocation-failure paths and SDDL conversions, which were windows-namespace-request-sys's security module until DI-14.8.1 moved them. An allocation that fails is an error the caller receives, never a panic or an abort. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format.
notCoveredHere: SecurityDescriptor::try_clone's failure is a declared blind spot (see its survives entry): AlignedBuf::try_clone allocates exactly the size of a buffer that already exists, so no test can make it fail. The failures of the two descriptor allocations, in capture and in conversion, are reached through their shared function, `allocate`, which the tests call with a length no machine has; the OS names the real length, so no descriptor can be made to ask for it. The descriptor's own parsing by Windows is not covered: what Windows accepts is Windows' to say.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a descriptor allocation failure is reported as an invalid copy
sabotages.why: An allocation failure is its own failure, SecurityCaptureFailure::Allocate: an invalid copy would send a caller looking for a malformed descriptor.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a descriptor allocation failure carries the wrong code
sabotages.why: The error's raw code is ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, which a caller who funnels everything through raw_os_error reads as 'out of memory'.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a copy of security attributes drops the descriptor
sabotages.why: A copy that kept the inheritance choice but not the descriptor would open files with different security than the original.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a descriptor alignment that is not a power of two is refused by the build
sabotages.why: AlignedBuf refuses such an alignment and `allocate` reports every refusal as an allocation failure, so a bad constant would read as out of memory on every call. The constant is asserted where it is defined.

sabotages.name: NR-3: BLIND SPOT: a failed copy of a descriptor is reported as an invalid copy
sabotages.why: Declared blind spot, not a control. SecurityDescriptor::try_clone allocates exactly the size of a buffer that already exists, so no test can make it fail; the failure it would report is the shared `allocation()`, whose result the other entries pin.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: a string is parsed at a revision Windows does not define
sabotages.why: SDDL_REVISION_1 is the one revision there is; any other is refused, so every string would be.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: a descriptor is written at a revision Windows does not define
sabotages.why: As for parsing: the revision names the text format, and only one is defined.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: a string with an interior NUL is passed to Windows
sabotages.why: Windows reads up to the NUL, so the string would be accepted as a different, shorter descriptor than it says.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: the interior-NUL refusal carries a different code
sabotages.why: The refusal is made here, not by Windows, and its code is ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, which a caller reads as it would Windows' own for a malformed string.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: a string Windows refuses is reported as a failure to write one
sabotages.why: The two directions have their own failure, which a caller tells apart.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: BLIND SPOT: a descriptor Windows refuses to write is reported as a refused string
sabotages.why: Declared blind spot, not a control. No descriptor and mask were found that Windows refuses to write, so the failure's kind cannot be reached from a test; the code it carries is read the same way as for parsing, which the other entries pin.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: the mask asked for is not the mask passed
sabotages.why: The mask is which parts of the descriptor are written; passing another writes the wrong parts.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: the text includes its terminator
sabotages.why: The text is the string and no more; a NUL on its end is a string no one wrote, and the reported length is not what tells it (it was measured to vary).

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: the text loses its last character
sabotages.why: The other half: a count one short cuts the string, which a length that does not count the terminator would do.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: the group is named as the owner
sabotages.why: Each part has its own bit, and the names are the values Windows defines.
replace: pub const GROUP: Self = Self(GROUP_SECURITY_INFORMATION | OWNER_SECURITY_INFORMATION);

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: a selection contains only what overlaps it
sabotages.why: A selection contains another when every bit of it is set, and everything contains none.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: BLIND SPOT: the memory Windows allocated is not freed
sabotages.why: Declared blind spot, not a control. A leak of this size is not observable from a test; the free is read from the code, which frees on every path through a guard.

sabotages.name: NR-3.1: control, the null check written as a comparison of the address
sabotages.why: A control: a pointer is null when its address is zero, so the file changes and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.2: a refused query is reported as success
sabotages.why: Windows answers with its own code and the descriptor is only valid when that is success; a query that read nothing must not become an empty descriptor.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.2: a refused query carries a code that is not Windows'
sabotages.why: The caller acts on the code Windows refused with; access denied and a bad parameter are different answers.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.2: the selection asked for is not the selection passed
sabotages.why: Which parts are read is the caller's choice; reading the DACL whatever was asked for hands back parts that were not selected.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.2: the kind of object asked for is not the kind passed
sabotages.why: The kind goes to Windows as named: a kind Windows refuses must still be refused, and not replaced by one it accepts.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.2: the file kind names the kernel object kind's value
sabotages.why: Each kind is the Win32 value it is named for; the constants are what a caller passes to Windows.

sabotages.name: review: a self-relative descriptor is copied by the length Windows reports
sabotages.why: The reported length counts the parts and says nothing about where they are: with a shared SID the copy reads past the source (the guard page faults), and with a gap it names a part outside itself. This is the code the review found.

sabotages.name: review: the safe query passes every kind
sabotages.why: A kind that does not match the handle is not always refused by Windows; the safe entry must refuse it before the call.

sabotages.name: review: the share kind is counted among those that read any handle
sabotages.why: LMSHARE with a file handle was measured faulting; the set the safe entry passes is the measured one and nothing more.

sabotages.name: review: control -- the kinds that read any handle are listed in another order
sabotages.why: Control. The same set, so the classification and refusal tests must not fire on it.
